A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DreamVLA study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original CALVIN evaluations, real-robot manipulation results, component ablations, and qualitative predictions.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds LIBERO evaluations and an inference-latency experiment.

M1.justification: The encoders, GPT-2 backbone, dynamic/depth/semantic queries, structured attention, prediction losses, and diffusion action decoder are retained. Appendix B.5 discusses possible latency optimizations without establishing an implemented method change.

E1.justification: v3 adds LIBERO-90 pretraining and evaluations on LIBERO-Spatial, Object, Goal, and Long, substantially broadening simulation coverage across spatial reasoning, object manipulation, and goal-oriented tasks. CALVIN, DROID, and the real-world pick/place/drawer tasks remain.

E2.justification: CALVIN Table 1 adds Pi0. The new LIBERO comparison includes SpatialVLA and CoT-VLA, which were cited but not evaluated in v1, alongside Diffusion Policy, Octo, and OpenVLA. Existing CALVIN and real-world comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds LIBERO-90 pretraining followed by suite-specific fine-tuning and a two-camera timing protocol comparing inference with and without dream queries. Section 4.1 changes the stated batch size from 8 to 64, aligning with both versions' appendix specification of 8 per GPU and 64 effective; this does not establish a changed training budget or rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.5 and Table 13 analyze computational overhead by removing dream queries and separating encoder, backbone, and action-head latency. The original knowledge-component, reconstruction-versus-prediction, optical-flow, attention, query-sharing, and query-count ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 13 newly states that inference timing was measured five times and averaged. This repetition information concerns the added timing experiment; policy-training seed counts, confidence intervals, and error bars are not added.

E6.justification: v3 adds a substantial LIBERO result set: DreamVLA scores 97.5, 94.0, 89.5, and 89.5 across the four suites, averaging 92.6%. It also adds Pi0's CALVIN results and timing measurements of 91 ms with dream queries versus 88 ms without. Retained CALVIN, real-world, ablation, and qualitative results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Equations 1–10, including the ELBO discussion, prediction objectives, diffusion loss, and combined loss, are retained. No new formal assumptions, definitions, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same perception–prediction–action framing, comprehensive forecasting contribution, and structured-attention/diffusion design claims. The headline CALVIN average length of 4.44 and real-world success rate of 76.7% also remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B.5 newly interprets dream-query overhead as small and identifies the action head as the main latency bottleneck. It discusses fewer sampling steps, smaller decoders, query pruning, and asynchronous execution for latency-sensitive applications. Existing mechanism explanations and manipulation-scope limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 documents LIBERO-90 pretraining and the RTX 4090, two-camera inference measurement setup. Its main-text batch-size statement now agrees with the existing effective-batch specification. Architecture tables, other training details, and project/code/model access links are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 expands its discussion into language plans, latent actions, visual rollouts, and object-centric predictions. References added include GR00T N1, SmolVLA, TraceVLA, FAST, ChatVLA, OneTwoVLA, Hi Robot, and LIBERO; Moto is removed. The central positioning around compact, comprehensive future knowledge remains.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites related-work and simulation-results passages, adds the inference-latency subsection, makes terminology and grammar edits, and adds coauthor Fan Lu. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds LIBERO Table 2 and latency Table 13, expands CALVIN Table 1, and redistributes existing tables across pages. Figure 6 gains previously missing category labels, and Figure 4 changes 'Segment' to 'Semantic'. Existing diagrams and qualitative examples are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The added LIBERO evaluation broadens empirical support, the controlled latency breakdown substantiates efficiency claims, and Figure 6's restored labels improve interpretability. Gains are limited by inconsistencies in new aggregates: CoT-VLA's displayed suite scores average 86.95%, versus the reported 69.0%, and Pi0's cumulative success rates imply 3.835 tasks, versus 3.92. The broader evidence and clearer presentation nevertheless support a modest net improvement.
